clue.text: Baptist may have a celebratory drink

definitions.text: Baptist may have a celebratory drink

parts.words: Baptist may have a celebratory drink
parts.note: one who baptises literally moistens an infant's crown, while the same phrase is the idiom for toasting a newborn with drinks

explanation.walkthrough: The British idiom for drinking to a new baby's health doubles as a literal description of a christening, where the person baptising sprinkles water on the infant's head.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names the toast fathers and friends drink to celebrate a birth, and literally describes christening water.

clue.text: Announced entrance as preliminary to fight

indicators.note: announced means spoken out, so the words for an entrance are heard as a homophone

parts.note: a way in is an entrance

explanation.surface: Fighters' entrance is announced before a bout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as' is a link. WAY IN, said out, sounds like the boxers' pre-fight session on the scales.
explanation.definitionFit: Boxers stand on the scales at a ceremony held before a bout to confirm their weight.

clue.text: Recorder has to come to the point

definitions.meaning: a person or machine that records on tape
to narrow gradually to a tip

explanation.walkthrough: 'has to' is a link; the recorder is read as someone who tapes, not the woodwind instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: To narrow to a tip is the verb sense; a person who tapes things is the noun sense.

clue.text: One involved with the beginning of antiquity, in short?

definitions.text: One involved with the beginning of antiquity, in short?

parts.words: One involved with the beginning of antiquity, in short?
parts.note: a scholar of the past is involved with antiquity from its start, and the question mark hints at a playful reading

explanation.definitionFit: A scholar who studies and writes about the past is involved with antiquity.

clue.text: Tempt cricketer to grab a single

indicators.note: to grab means the cricketer takes hold of the other piece, which ends up inside

parts.note: a bat is a batsman in cricket
I, the Roman numeral, is a single one

explanation.surface: Lure a batsman into going for a quick single run.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a 'single' is one run; here it is just the numeral I.
explanation.definitionFit: To lure or entice someone, as fishermen do with worms on hooks.

clue.text: Swell the uproar

definitions.meaning: a swell is a grand, important person

explanation.definitionFit: An important, influential person is a swell or bigwig, and a loud din is literally that.

clue.text: Scottish island has lost a lot of workers

indicators.note: has lost means the island's name drops the following letter

parts.note: Staffa is a small Hebridean island, home to Fingal's Cave

explanation.surface: Many workers have left a Scottish island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has lost' drops A from STAFFA, the Inner Hebrides island famous for Fingal's Cave.
explanation.definitionFit: The employees of an organisation are collectively its personnel.

clue.text: Softening the speaker up, till one breaks

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word for the speaker is read bottom to top

parts.note: me is the speaker referring to themselves

indicators.note: breaks means the letters of the following words are shattered and reassembled

explanation.surface: A soothing balm works on a talker until somebody cracks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns ME into EM; 'breaks' rearranges TILL and ONE into OLLIENT.
explanation.definitionFit: An emollient cream soothes and softens the skin.

clue.text: Senior member managed without money out East

indicators.note: without in its old sense means outside, so the word for managed goes round the money

parts.note: done can mean managed or accomplished
the yen is Japan's currency

explanation.surface: An elder managed with no cash while out in the East.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' here is the old sense, outside, not 'lacking': the word for managed goes round the money.
explanation.definitionFit: A doyenne is the most respected or longest-serving woman in a group.

clue.text: One new dad's got to celebrate, incidentally

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
pa is another word for dad, with the possessive giving the S
to sing is to celebrate, as in singing someone's praises

explanation.surface: A first-time father has to mark the occasion, mentioned only in passing.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying something by the way, as a casual aside, means mentioning it incidentally.

clue.text: The pain of Carroll's fits

definitions.meaning: Lewis Carroll subtitled his poem The Hunting of the Snark 'An ... in Eight Fits', fits being its cantos

explanation.walkthrough: 'of' is a link. Carroll called the cantos of his Snark poem fits, and the whole an agony in eight of them.
explanation.definitionFit: Intense suffering is anguish, and Carroll used the word for his eight-canto nonsense poem.

clue.text: School in distress

definitions.meaning: A famous English public school in north-west London

explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link. HARROW is one of England's best-known fee-paying schools.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to torment or trouble someone, and it is also the name of an English public school.

clue.text: Waving no flag and no banner

indicators.note: waving suggests the letters fluttering about and so being rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone flies no flag and carries no banner at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Waving' rearranges NO, FLAG and NO together; 'and' joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A gonfalon is a flag hung from a crossbar, a kind of standard or banner.

clue.text: It's seen on laptop after selection from menu

definitions.text: It's seen on laptop after selection from menu

parts.words: It's seen on laptop after selection from menu
parts.note: laptop is read as the top of a diner's lap, where a cloth is spread once the meal has been ordered from the menu, not a portable computer

explanation.walkthrough: 'laptop' and 'menu' paint a computer screen; the lap's top is where a diner spreads a cloth after ordering.
explanation.definitionFit: A table cloth for wiping the mouth sits on the diner's lap during a meal.

clue.text: Eliminate a language? That's not on

parts.note: Polish is the language of Poland
off means not on, as a switch is

explanation.surface: Someone wants to stamp out a language, protesting that it's unacceptable.
explanation.definitionFit: To finish off or get rid of something completely, as of food or an opponent.

clue.text: Sweatier_after excitement, so to speak

indicators.note: excitement stirs things up, so the letters of the preceding word are shaken into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone is sweatier after getting excited, to put it a certain way.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases are fillers signalling that the words are used loosely or figuratively.

clue.text: Sea water making odd holes in canvas

indicators.note: in says the scrambled letters are placed inside the canvas shelter

parts.note: a tent is made of canvas

indicators.note: making odd means the letters are turned strange, rearranged

explanation.surface: Seawater gets through strange holes in a canvas sail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'making odd' signals the anagram and 'in' the container. THE SOLENT is the strait between the Isle of Wight and the English mainland, not open sea.
explanation.definitionFit: The Solent is a channel of the English Channel separating the Isle of Wight from Hampshire.

clue.text: Singer's visibly embarrassed and shy

definitions.note: read as 'singer is', the possessive giving 'is'

parts.note: someone blushing turns red
to shy, like a horse, is to start or jump back in alarm

explanation.surface: A performer blushes and is bashful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shy' looks like an adjective but is the verb, as a horse shies or starts; a redstart is a small songbird.
explanation.definitionFit: The redstart is a songbird with a rust-red tail, so a singer in crossword terms.

clue.text: It can strain an officer accompanying sovereign

parts.note: Col is the abbreviation for colonel, an army officer
and means along with, accompanying
ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the queen

explanation.surface: A soldier in the company of the monarch might feel the strain.
explanation.definitionFit: A colander is a perforated bowl used to drain or sieve food.

clue.text: Second ingredient changed in apple sauce

indicators.note: the second ingredient is the second letter of the word, and changed says it is swapped for another

parts.note: costard is an old English variety of cooking apple

explanation.surface: A cook alters the second component of an apple sauce.
explanation.walkthrough: COSTARD is an old English apple; changing its second letter O to U gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Custard is a sweet yellow pouring sauce served with puddings.

clue.text: A penguin has intelligence also

parts.note: gen is British slang for information or intelligence
too means also

explanation.surface: A clever penguin is credited with brains as well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has' is a link; GEN is British slang for the information one is given.
explanation.definitionFit: The gentoo is a species of penguin with a white stripe across its head.

clue.text: Behind schedule with deliveries? Exactly!

parts.note: in cricket an over is a set of six deliveries by one bowler
due means exactly, as in due north

explanation.surface: A courier complains that a parcel is late, and someone agrees emphatically.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' is a link. 'deliveries' suggests parcels but is cricket's balls bowled.
explanation.definitionFit: Something late, past the time it was expected, is tardy or belated.

clue.text: Sort of account that grips an audience

definitions.meaning: in bookkeeping a ... account holds sums awaiting allocation
tension that keeps viewers on the edge of their seats

explanation.definitionFit: Tension that holds an audience is this quality, and accountants keep a holding ledger of the same name.

clue.text: Half-heartedly worry over Scottish town

indicators.note: over means the word is turned upside down, read backwards in a down clue
half-heartedly means one of the two central letters of the word is removed

parts.note: to niggle is to worry or nag

explanation.surface: Someone frets mildly about a town in Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Half-heartedly' drops one of the middle Gs of NIGGLE to give NIGLE, and 'over' turns it into the Moray town.
explanation.definitionFit: Elgin is a cathedral town in Moray, in north-east Scotland.

clue.text: It's sweet, but one can't operate effectively for it

definitions.meaning: a chewy confection of boiled sugar and butter

definitions.text: one can't operate effectively for it
definitions.meaning: the British idiom says someone who cannot do something well cannot do it for this sweet

explanation.walkthrough: 'but' is a link. The British phrase 'can't do it for toffee' means to be hopeless at something.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a chewy boiled sugar sweet, and the idiom 'can't do it for toffee' means utterly incompetent.

clue.text: Country short of English money

indicators.note: short of means lacking, so the country loses a letter

parts.note: France is a country

explanation.surface: A nation is running low on English currency.
explanation.definitionFit: The franc was the currency of France before the euro and is still Swiss currency.

clue.text: Person transforming text, say, for end of book

indicators.note: say signals that the word for the person is spoken out and heard as another

parts.note: a coder turns plain text into code

explanation.surface: A text editor reaches the final pages of a book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' is a link; in non-rhotic British speech CODER sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A coda is a concluding section, of music or of a literary work.

clue.text: Surrounded by characters from team on guard

indicators.note: characters from says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A sentry is surrounded by members of the team keeping watch.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's definition 'Surrounded' alone is a participle, not a preposition; 'Surrounded by' swaps for the answer, so 'by' belongs in the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in the midst of a group is to be encircled by its members.

clue.text: A lot of trees cut down with help, as mentioned previously

indicators.note: cut down means trimmed short, so the last letter of the wood is lopped

parts.note: a forest is a large number of trees
aid means help

explanation.surface: A woodland is felled with assistance, as noted earlier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut down' removes the final T of FOREST to leave FORES; 'with' and 'as' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Legal writing uses the word for something already referred to earlier in the text.

clue.text: The entail certified as broken

indicators.note: broken says the letters of the two words are smashed and put back together differently

explanation.surface: A legal entail is broken, as a certificate shows.
explanation.definitionFit: In grammar 'the' is the classic example of this part of speech, the specifying determiner.
